transcript.content: Hello, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?
I guess… I’m here because I just can’t seem to settle. It feels like I’m crawling out of my own skin, like I need to get up and do the next thing, even when I’m exhausted and should be sitting still.
Did this feeling start after you began taking an antidepressant or after the dose was changed?
I’m not really sure. I don’t think I noticed it starting right after anything like that… but I’d have to think about it.
When you do sleep, do you feel like you need much less sleep than usual?
I don’t know… I mean, I sleep when I can. I haven’t really noticed needing less than usual, exactly.
Does this feeling come in sudden attacks that peak within minutes?
I don’t think so… not like an attack. It’s more just… there. But I’m not sure.
When you feel this way, do you have a strong inner urge to keep moving?
Yes… I guess that’s a big part of it. I feel like I can’t settle inside myself, like I have to get up and do the next thing even when I’m tired and should just sit still.
Did this restless feeling begin soon after you started an antidepressant or increased the dose?
I’m not really sure. I don’t remember it starting right after something like that… I just haven’t kept track very well.
Are you currently taking an antidepressant?
I’m… not sure. I’d have to check the names of what I’m taking.
Could you check whether one of your current medications is an antidepressant?
I… I don’t have the list with me right now. I’d need to look at the bottles or maybe ask the pharmacy. I’m not sure offhand.
During this period, have you felt unusually euphoric or excessively high?
I don’t think so… not really. I can’t say I’ve felt unusually high or anything like that.
When you feel this restlessness, do you also feel worried or anxious?
I don’t know if I’d call it worried exactly. It’s more like… I can’t settle inside myself. Like I need to get up and do the next thing, even when I’m tired and should be sitting still.
When you feel this way, do you find yourself pacing or unable to keep your legs still?
Yes… my legs don’t stay still much. I’ll tap my foot or shift around, even at church meetings. Sometimes I catch myself rubbing the edge of my purse, and people next to me start noticing.
Before this restless feeling began, had you started taking an antidepressant?
I’m not sure… I don’t think there was anything like that, but I’d have to think about it.
Have you started or increased an antidepressant in the past few weeks?
I don’t really know. I can’t say that I remember starting or changing anything like that recently.
Do you spend a lot of time worrying about many different things?
I don’t know… I wouldn’t say a lot. I think about things, sure, but I’m not sure I’d call it worrying about everything.
Does the restless feeling come with a sense of nervousness?
Yeah… I guess it’s kind of like nervousness, but more like I just can’t settle in my own skin. Like I need to get up and do something, even when I’m tired.
Before this restless feeling started, were you taking an antidepressant?
I’m not really sure. I don’t remember being on one before it started, but… I could be forgetting.
Have you taken any antidepressant medication in the past month?
I’m not sure… I don’t think so, but I’d have to check.
Have you taken any antidepressant medicine in the last month?
I… I really don’t think so, but I’m not completely sure. I’d probably need to look at my bottles or paperwork.
Do you feel this restlessness because your mind is stuck worrying?
Not exactly worrying, no. It’s more like… I can’t settle in my own skin. Like I have to get up and do the next thing, even when I’m worn out and should just sit still.
Do you spend much of the day worrying a lot?
I don’t know… I wouldn’t say most of the day, no. I get bothered by things, but I’m not sure I’d call it worrying a lot.
